pages.seoDescription: A café in Jhamsikhel, Lalitpur. Hand-folded momo, coffee from Nuwakot and Gulmi roasted in-house every Tuesday, Thakali set on Saturdays. Open daily from 7:30.

props.text: Beans from Nuwakot and Gulmi, roasted here every Tuesday. Momo folded from six each morning. Chiya until the last guest leaves.

props.name: Sarita Maharjan

props.heading: Three things we do the long way

image.alt: Steam rising from a basket of momo, with tomato achar on the side

items.title: Momo, folded from six every morning
items.text: Buff, chicken, or mushroom and cheese, wrapped by Maili Didi and two helpers before the doors open. Steamed, jhol, or kothey with a crisp base. The achar is roasted tomato, timur and sesame, ground on a stone.

image.alt: Hot water poured in a slow circle over a paper coffee filter

items.title: Pour-over from two Nepali hillsides
items.text: Washed arabica from a farmers’ cooperative in Nuwakot and a family estate in Gulmi. We roast light so you can taste the place: stone fruit from one, brown sugar and cocoa from the other.

image.alt: A tray of small glasses of masala chiya, ready to go out

items.title: Masala chiya, boiled the old way
items.text: Assam CTC, fresh ginger, green cardamom and a pinch of black pepper, boiled twice with full-cream milk. The first cup at 7:30 on Sunday is on the house.

props.intro: Most coffee sold in Kathmandu left the farm a year ago. Ours left in the last month.

props.heading: Saturday is Thakali day
props.body:
Rice from Jumla, black dal cooked for three hours in a copper pot, gundruk, seasonal saag, timur and tomato achar, and chicken or mutton curry. Everything is refilled until you tell us to stop.

We make sixty sets. Book a table if you are coming after one o’clock.

props.heading: Before you order
props.intro: Ask at the counter too. We would rather cook it your way than have you go without.

items.a: Yes. The mushroom momo can be made without cheese, the dal, saag and achar are vegan, and every coffee comes with oat milk if you ask.

items.q: Can I get momo to take away?
items.a: Yes, cooked or frozen. Frozen momo come in packs of fifty and keep for a month.

items.q: Is there a charge for sitting and working?
items.a: No. There are sockets under the window bench and the Wi-Fi password is on your bill. On weekend afternoons we ask laptops to share tables.

items.q: Do you take eSewa and Khalti?
items.a: Yes, and Fonepay QR, cards and cash.

pages.title: Our coffee
pages.seoTitle: Nepali coffee roasted in Jhamsikhel · Ghumti Café
pages.seoDescription: Washed arabica from Nuwakot and Gulmi, roasted every Tuesday in Jhamsikhel. Buy 250 g and 500 g bags or a monthly bag delivered in the valley.

props.title: Coffee from two Nepali hillsides, roasted twelve kilos at a time
props.text: We buy directly from a farmers’ cooperative in Nuwakot and one family estate in Gulmi, pay above the Fairtrade floor, and roast every Tuesday in the room behind the counter.

image.alt: Ripe red coffee cherries on a branch

props.heading: Why Nepali coffee
props.body:
Nepal grows very little coffee, about five hundred tonnes a year, most of it on small terraces between 1,000 and 1,700 metres. That is the height where arabica ripens slowly and tastes of something.

For years most of it left the country as green beans. We would rather you drank it here, fresh, and knew whose field it came from. Every bag we sell says the farm, the harvest month and the roast date.

image.alt: Coffee cherries ripening on the plant

items.title: Nuwakot, Kakani ridge, 1,700 m
items.text: Forty families sell through the Kakani cooperative. Washed and dried on raised beds. In the cup: apricot, black tea, a clean finish. Harvest December and January.

image.alt: Medium-roasted coffee beans

items.title: Gulmi, Arkhale, 1,300 m
items.text: The Bhandari family estate, three hectares under alder shade. Pulped natural. In the cup: brown sugar, cocoa, a heavier body that loves milk. Harvest November.

items.title: Picked
items.text: Only ripe red cherries, by hand, over several passes of each tree.

items.title: Processed at the farm
items.text: Pulped, fermented and washed or dried in the fruit, then rested in parchment.

items.title: Roasted in Jhamsikhel
items.text: Twelve kilos a batch, light for filter, medium for espresso.

items.title: Rested and packed
items.text: Five days of rest, then into valve bags with the roast date written by hand.
